name: Electron
tagline: A framework for building desktop applications with Chromium, Node.js, and web technologies.
hook: A guide to multi-repository builds, patches, C++ object lifetimes, release maintenance, and alternatives to costly commands.
summary: Electron's CLAUDE.md explains its multi-repository build and patch process, garbage-collected C++ objects, and release maintenance. Several familiar commands are forbidden because the repository has safer or cheaper alternatives.

techniques.title: Use the result CI has already produced
techniques.body: For patch conflicts on an existing PR, the guide first checks the failed Apply Patches run for an exported resolution. A local three-way sync is the fallback when the artifact is absent.
techniques.quote: If asked to fix a patch conflict on a branch that already has an open PR, check the PR's failed **Apply Patches** CI run for an `update-patches.patch` artifact before running `e sync` locally.

techniques.title: Give a prohibition a concrete replacement
techniques.body: The file bans npx because it may fetch and execute an uninstalled package. It offers a direct node_modules binary or Yarn invocation instead, applying the same restriction to commands and authored scripts.
techniques.quote: **Never use `npx`.** It is considered dangerous because it can silently fetch and execute arbitrary packages from the registry.

techniques.title: Explain ownership constraints in the garbage collector
techniques.body: The C++ guidance distinguishes heap edges, roots, and native stack locals. It connects tracing omissions to use-after-free and explains why destructors cannot inspect other managed objects.
techniques.quote:
Destructors must not access other GC managed objects: sweeping has no object
  destruction order or timing guarantee.

techniques.title: Apply release labels only to users with write access
techniques.body: Labeling guidance is explicitly scoped to contributors with repository write access. It distinguishes ordinary bug-fix backports from security fixes and derives active branches from label metadata instead of a copied release list.

techniques.title: Select upgrade skills from the active branch
techniques.body: Chromium and Node.js upgrades have separate named skills and branch triggers. The branch is the concrete signal for which specialized workflow to load.
techniques.quote: When working on the `roller/chromium/main` branch to upgrade Chromium activate the "Electron Chromium Upgrade" skill.

steal: Check whether CI already produced the expensive local operation's result.
Pair forbidden commands with approved alternatives and a reason.
Explain ownership and destruction-order assumptions near memory rules.
State which release actions require repository permissions.
